raw_text:
Alright, Thursday, Nov 12, 2026. Grab a coffee, let's get into it.

---

Money Talk

- **Jensen Huang's AI Kingdom Crumbles, $888B Gone**
  Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang finally resigned after the second affair allegation dropped – this one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has nuked Nvidia's value by an eye-watering $888 billion this week alone, raising serious questions about the AI economy's "central bank." CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and President Trump is hilariously pitching Tim Cook for the top job. Wild. [S7][S8][S9][S11][S12][S15][S19][S52]

- **Fed Plays Hot and Cold on Rates**
  In a bizarre move, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced the October 2027 meeting won't even *see* a vote on interest rates, hinting at a policy switch. Meanwhile, on the ground, the Fed is facing mounting pressure for *more* rate hikes now as inflation isn't chilling out and is spreading beyond "trouble spots." Pick a lane, guys. [S1][S18]

- **Housing Market Hits 16-Year Low**
  If you're trying to buy a house, you already know. Existing home sales in October hit a 16-year low, dropping 8.8% year-on-year. Record-high mortgage rates and persistent inflation are just nuking demand. It's rough out there. [S13]

- **Oil Jitters After Trump's Iran Comments**
  Crude prices were mixed today after President Trump declared "We've got their Strait" and said no Iran deal was needed. Sounds like the U.S.-Iran standoff isn't ending soon, keeping oil traders on edge. [S2]

- **UK Car Industry Demands EV Tariff Delay**
  The UK car industry is pleading with the EU for a two-year delay on post-Brexit EV tariffs. New "rules of origin" on batteries are set to kick in January 1st, potentially making UK-EU EV trade a lot more expensive. Nobody wants to pay more for their electric Mini, do they? [S14]

World Lore

- **US Envoys Shuttle Between Putin and Zelenskyy**
  Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were spotted in the Kremlin, briefing Putin after initial Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi. Now they're off to Ireland for talks with Zelenskyy. It's a high-stakes diplomatic relay, though the Abu Dhabi talks mostly just managed a prisoner exchange. Baby steps, I guess? [S21][S24][S25][S33]

- **Indonesia VP Resigns Over Questionable Degree**
  Indonesia's Vice President Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, just resigned. Turns out his overseas academic credentials didn't meet election requirements, according to the Constitutional and Supreme Courts. Can't fake it till you make it when you're VP, apparently. [S22]

- **EU Takes On Digital Dark Patterns**
  Good news for your sanity: the EU is pushing for a Digital Fairness Act to curb everything from those sneaky subscription traps to misleading sales tactics and features designed to keep you doom-scrolling. Hopefully, it'll make online life less of a constant battle against manipulation. [S31]

- **Europe's Schools Hit By Hoax Bomb Threats**
  Hundreds of schools across Europe have been targeted by hoax bomb threats, leading authorities to suspect it's another round of hybrid warfare. Classrooms becoming targets in a geopolitical game? Not a good look. [S29]

- **Hungary Makes Unexpected Shift on Abortion Rights**
  In a surprising break from its conservative past, Hungary is easing abortion restrictions and scrapping the controversial "heartbeat regulation." The reforms also aim to better protect women against violence. A rare progressive move from that corner of Europe. [S34]

Tech Tea

- **Jensen Huang's Capitol Hill Debut Looms**
  The Nvidia drama continues: Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before US Congress after threats of a subpoena. His departure, tied to allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, means the world's second-most valuable company is now under a massive geopolitical microscope. This isn't just a corporate scandal anymore. [S45][S47][S52]

- **Cybertruck Bites the Dust, Fans Revolt**
  It's official: Elon Musk has pulled the plug on the Cybertruck. This isn't sitting well with the legions of diehard fans who built their online identities around the polarizing pickup. Usually, they'd defend Musk, but this time, the cyber-pitchforks are out. [S48]

- **AI Chatbots Caught Recommending Fake Retail Sites**
  Beware of shopping advice from your favorite AI. A new study found that chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini are directing users to imposters and other risky websites when asked for product info. Great, another way AI can accidentally scam you. [S50]

- **United Airlines Bans AI Booking Agents**
  In a move citing cybersecurity risks, United Airlines announced it won't allow customers to use AI agents to book flights or manage reservations. Looks like some industries are taking a "slow down, AI" approach to avoid potential headaches. [S42]

- **SoftBank's Billion-Dollar AI Energy Blunder**
  Looks like SoftBank took a big swing and missed. They've reportedly lost over $3 billion pre-ordering natural gas turbines to power AI data centers. Turns out, powering the AI boom isn't cheap or easy, and SoftBank's mega-bet just put a cap on some of those "AI needs endless energy" ambitions. [S43]

Creator Szn

- **Yahoo Licenses "Spotify-Like" AI Content Model**
  Yahoo is the first big player to sign on with the Internet Licensing Collective, essentially a "Spotify for AI content." This model aims to give publishers a new way to get paid when AI search models hoover up their content. Good luck monetizing the robots, folks. [S56]

- **Brands Now Greenlighting Creator TV Shows**
  Forget sponsored posts – brands like Anthropologie are now commissioning full-blown creator-created shows. It's a clear signal that the creator economy is maturing, with brands seeking deeper, more engaging content than just another TikTok. [S59]

- **TwitchCon: Is the Party Over?**
  Ahead of TwitchCon 2026, creators and brands are publicly questioning if the annual IRL event is worth the cost and potential safety issues. Sounds like TwitchCon might be at a crossroads, needing to prove its value to the very community it champions. [S60]

- **LinkedIn Expands B2B Ads to UK Connected TVs**
  LinkedIn is stepping well beyond the job board, bringing its B2B ad targeting capabilities to connected TVs in the UK. Because nothing says "enterprise solutions" like seeing your CRM ad pop up during your binge-watch. [S58]

- **AI Measurement Standards Remain Elusive for Publishers**
  The IAB's new AI attribution framework was supposed to standardize how AI's impact is measured, but publishers are still struggling. Turns out, platform data gaps are making much of AI's actual value invisible. Classic tech, all hype, no clear ROI data. [S57]

Supply Lines

- **DHL Boosts Stockholm, Goes Green in Paris**
  DHL Express is dropping €55 million on a new Stockholm gateway, expanding its reach. On the sustainability front, they're the first express cargo carrier to use Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) at Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport. Respect the results, indeed. [S78][S80]
- **Amazon Doubles Down on Same-Day, But Sparks NYC Labor Row**
  Amazon just launched a new facility in Daytona Beach for same-day delivery and raised its game in Brussels to same-day by 3 p.m. killer for local logistics. But in NYC, a partner company for Amazon deliveries just fired 200 e-bike workers, sparking debate about Amazon's delivery model. [S86][S88][S89]
- **Shippers Warned to Prep for UPS 2028 Teamsters Clash**
  The UPS Teamsters contract doesn't expire until 2028, but experts are already telling shippers to diversify their carrier relationships *now*. The memory of last year's negotiation jitters is fresh, and nobody wants to be caught off guard by a potential strike again. Plan ahead or get cooked. [S67]
- **Trump's Tariff Threats vs. Congressional Pushback**
  President Trump is back at it, threatening to double tariffs on Mexican imports over alleged migrant influx. Meanwhile, Congress is trying to rein him in, with three separate bills aiming to restrict presidential tariff power. It's a classic D.C. showdown with real implications for cross-border freight. [S62][S68]
- **Ocean Freight: Profits Soar, Ports Jam, Fleet Transforms**
  Hapag-Lloyd just reported soaring profits thanks to strong freight rates, despite flat volumes. But the party isn't everywhere: Spanish box terminals are facing backlogs after a general strike. Looking ahead, a wave of massive newbuild containerships is set to render the aging panamax fleet commercially obsolete by 2030. The seas, they are a-changin'. [S72][S73][S74]

Speed Round

- Ukraine says Starshield was throttled again, SpaceX denies it.
- One dead, four injured in a Logan Circle shooting; suspect is also dead.
- Mercedes-Benz froze German investments due to pressure from unions.
- Sri Lanka's new "anti-terror" law is getting flak for being just as bad as the old one.
- Google DeepMind employees are taking their unionization fight to the UK government.
- Xbox is apparently trying to reinvent itself for the umpteenth time after 25 years.
- Turns out AI models *know* about women, peace, and security, they just don't bring it up unprompted.
